name: Abū Muḥammad Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn al-Mawṣilī
summary: Musician and man of letters of the ʿAbbāsid court, pupil of al-Aṣmaʿī and Abū ʿUbayda, whom Ibn al-Anbārī includes for his learning in the language and poetry.
bio: Isḥāq learned letters from al-Aṣmaʿī, Abū ʿUbayda and others, but the art of singing came to dominate him and he became known by it; Ibn al-Anbārī names a Kitāb al-Aghānī as his. His son Ḥammād, Abū al-ʿAynāʾ and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār transmitted from him.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 227–232
